chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who struck a slave boy on the head, causing part of his tongue to be lost; he could articulate some speech but not all. He was asked to recite the 'Mujam' (a reference text, likely for pronunciation/diction), so the Commander of the Faithful divided the blood money upon him: whatever he could articulate clearly, he was exempted from paying for it, and whatever he could not articulate clearly, he was held liable for it.

key_terms.طَرَحَهُ: He exempted it / cast it aside

ai.seo_question: How is blood money calculated for partial loss of the tongue in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) in *Al-Istibsar* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *taqsim al-diyyah* (proportional division of blood money) applied to linguistic impairment. By testing the victim's ability to articulate specific phonemes, the Imam established a precise, empirical method for quantifying the loss of speech function, distinguishing between lost articulation and retained capacity. This approach underscores the practical application of justice in personal injury cases, ensuring compensation reflects the actual functional deficit rather than a fixed standard.
